what: dynamics library v1 + unit tests (exact damped-oscillator step, semi-implicit Euler, mass proxy, spring chain with PBD segments and collisions, hinge)
saw: 4 test failures: cloth/paper/foliage energy after 3 s above 1e-4 (the test ignored air drag), door hinge never came to rest (friction reversed sign every substep)
changed: test uses drag as added damping; static friction holds the hinge when the torque cannot overcome it

what: staging, before drawing: where the camera, door, person and dog can be so that the dog's head stays visible inside the doorway
saw: (worked out geometrically, not rendered) a 3/4 exterior view hides anything 0.4 m inside the door behind the near jamb; a side view needs the house in section; a door hinged on the near jamb ends up between the camera and the room
changed: side view with the house cut by the picture plane at the near jamb; glazed door hinged on the far jamb, opening inward so the open leaf becomes the lit backdrop; the person stands just inside and sits 1.1 m inside (the score has her at -1.25 m)

saw: staging reads; but ball joints at knees and elbows, a lumpy lying pose with a raised thigh ball, fur strokes far too long, the lit dog over-saturated orange, the treeline reads as mountains, light spill banded, the low hand rests on the knees, ears tiny
changed: upper legs merged into the torso silhouette, explicit sphinx joints for lying, stroke length tied to sphere radius, warm light clamped, canopies for trees, spill drawn as merged equal-visibility wedges, person sits cross-legged and reaches low, bigger ears
result: better; next looked at the turns

what: both turns frame by frame (3.33-3.92 s, 7.42-8.67 s)
saw: every frame reads as a dog (it passes through facing the camera, never edge-on); vertical stripe artifacts on the chest mid-turn; the head came round late (7.67 s) and pointed at the camera rather than the door; the lying head touched the planter
changed: coat proxy anchored on the neck base, not the head (head acceleration in the spin is ~20 m/s^2), offsets clamped to 2.5 cm; head comes round 7.458-7.64 to 2.45 rad; planter moved to the back corner with arching stems

what: full film v1, sound v1, checker
saw: check_handmade ALL OK (I3 r=1.0 on x_world_measured, I4 0.948); trace facing at 7.5-8.2 still -1 because it measures the head's position, not where it points
changed: trace gets head_facing from the drawn muzzle direction
result: head_facing flips toward the door at 7.583 s

saw: A5 failed: head above the back line for the first 4 approach frames (score head ramps 0.9 to 0.5 after the choice); A6 used crude onsets
changed: the head goes down as it decides to come (head anticipates the score's ramp by 9 frames, 14.3-15.3 s); onsets defined once for all choices: 2 cm of measured travel, or 25 % of a posture/head transition
result: A5 218/218 frames, worst margin 16.1 cm; A6 all onsets +0.08 to +0.14 s

what: collar tag: 1272 contacts in 32 s (up to 72 per second), i.e. a jingle stream
saw: a solver fault, not behaviour. Hypothesis 1 (impact speed in the world frame, not relative to the moving chest): fixed, no change. Hypothesis 2 (collar ring sinks inside the chest collider when the dog cowers): fixed, worse (48/s). Hypothesis 3 (pushing a node out of a boundary becomes outward velocity, a fake bounce): inelastic contact in the boundary's frame, 19/s left, exactly one per frame. Hypothesis 4 (anchors are interpolated across substeps but boundaries sat at end-of-frame positions)
changed: all four kept: boundaries carry velocity and are interpolated per substep, contact speed is relative, contacts are inelastic, the ring rides on the chest, contact events need an onset with 8 mm hysteresis
result: 15 tag contacts, all at real events (the flinch at the call, the refusal spin, lying down, the rise at 7.67 s); scarf min gap -1.6 mm became 0

saw: mid-turn the dog faced the camera: a viewer sees its face, not its back
changed: the refusal turns away from the viewer (rump and back come round to us); the turn back to look still goes through the camera side so the face comes round first
result: 3.6 s shows the dog from behind; 4.3 s the turned back; turn back reads frame by frame

what: the soundtrack, looked at as an RMS envelope (it cannot be listened to here)
saw: spikes to about -12 dBFS inside the soft lines at 8 s and 11 s: the 't'/'ts' consonant bursts were not scaled with the syllable's loudness
changed: consonants scale with the syllable; soft voice raised slightly
result: calls -13.8 dBFS RMS, soft voice -27.1 (13.3 dB quieter), room tone -51.0; peak soft -18 dBFS vs calls -4 to -5

what: damping presets in synchronized split view (proof/presets.mp4) and their numbers (proof/assertions.json)
saw: in stills the presets differ subtly; in numbers: after the wag the tail settles in 1.17 s with 2 swings (tuned) vs 3.42 s with 7 (underdamped); ears 0.83 s/2 vs 1.71 s/7; shrub 1.96 s/3 vs 5.08 s/11; no-secondary puts the tail 3.8 cm into the floor and the scarf 8.9 cm into the lap
changed: nothing; tuned is kept as the film

what: final pass: 28 frames across the scene, the four stills, the cards
saw: the choices read in my frames: backing away cowering, the rump and turned back, the head coming round, standing to watch in the light, coming head low, lying across the sill with forelegs and head inside the frame and the tail out on the boards, the head turning in to the lit room, chin down, staying. Weak: 0-6 s the dog is dim against the railing; the door's opening is mostly read through the light; the dog is ~250 px long in the wide shot
result: watchable; invariants hold; handed to the independent critic
